Public domain: every person whose words are in this text died in 1925 or earlier, so the term has ended under the law of every country, whichever one first published it.

People: Charlotte Brontë (author, Wikidata Q127332), died 1855; Anne Brontë (author, Wikidata Q44520), died 1849; Emily Brontë (author, Wikidata Q80137), died 1848. They are every person Project Gutenberg's catalog lists for the book ("Brontë, Charlotte, 1816-1855; Brontë, Anne, 1820-1849; Brontë, Emily, 1818-1848") and every person the printed edition's opening pages credit; each death year is Wikidata's.

Printed edition: The professor, by Charlotte Brontë (Currer Bell) and poems by Charlotte, Emily and Anne Brontë and the Rev. Patrick Brontë, etc. with an introduction by Mrs. Humphrey Ward, N.Y. : Harper & Bros., 1900, the Internet Archive scan https://archive.org/details/cu31924016652400. Three passages of the Gutenberg text have 95%, 96%, 93% of their four-word runs in the scan's text. The scan does not show the credit of Anne Brontë, Emily Brontë, whom the catalog lists; the passages show the scan holds this text.
